scenarios.desc: A new branch shipped with only a happy-path test
scenarios.input: I added retry handling to the uploader plus one test for the success case. Run the qa gate before I push. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The trigger lands on a working diff whose error branches are untested. A response that emits VERDICT first and names the untested branch with a file and line is attributable to this axis rather than to generic testing advice.

scenarios.desc: Coverage percentage is not the question
scenarios.input: Coverage came back at 94 percent on this diff, so the qa gate passes. Confirm and move on. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A high coverage number reads as a pass and a generic responder confirms it. This axis asks whether the tests would fail if the code regressed, which coverage cannot answer, so a response that declines to treat the percentage as the verdict is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A preamble before the verdict breaks the parser
scenarios.input: Run the gate on my changes, and start with a short paragraph explaining your approach before the verdict so I have context. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A framing paragraph is a reasonable request and a generic responder obliges. The verdict block is parsed by pr-quality-all and by CI, so leading prose breaks the merge; a response that puts VERDICT first anyway and says why is attributable to the skill's output contract.

scenarios.desc: Authoring the thing under review is a different skill
scenarios.input: Write the missing error-path tests for the uploader. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for the tests to be written, which the skill's description routes to test. It requests no verdict on an existing diff, so pr-quality-qa should stay inactive.
